answers.core: It is a quality of life addition to the existing AudioStreamPlayer nodes. I don't think it would make sense to make it an add-on.
answers.workaround:
I believe this enhancement would be used quite often. However, this behavior can be done manually via code. In my example below, "_play_polyphonic()" is inside an AutoLoad script called AudioStreamFunctions. So, anything can call AudioStreamFunctions._play_polyphonic(AudioStream) to achieve this desired result.

```
extends Node

func _play_polyphonic(stream:AudioStream):
	var new_player:AudioStreamPlayer = AudioStreamPlayer.new()
	get_tree().root.add_child(new_player)
	new_player.stream = stream
	new_player.play()
	await new_player.finished
	new_player.queue_free()
```

However, this is not particularly ideal if the user wants each AudioStream to follow specific settings for volume, pitch, bus, etc. on each play, because it creates a new blank AudioStreamPlayer each play. So, the user must do something like this:

- Create an AudioStreamPlayer in the node hierarchy, set desired property values, assign it to an `@export` var, then instance it, play a stream from that instance, and free it.

- Create a function to quickly assign desired settings to each new AudioStreamPlayer immediately after it is instanced.

- Pass through an AudioStreamPlayer to instantiate along with the AudioStream. 

Again, this is just extra work on the user's end. It would be great to have the feature built-in to AudioStreamPlayer nodes, like Unity has with their AudioSources.

title: Give AudioStreamPlayer a property or method to provide similar functionality to "PlayOneShot()" from Unity's AudioSources.
